newsitem.title: INDIA: India money supply up, call rates seen volatile.
newsitem.headline: India money supply up, call rates seen volatile.

text.p: Indian call money rates ruled below 6.0 percent levels for most part of the fortnight, but tax payout should see increased volatility in the call rates later in the month, ICICI Securities and Finance Company (I-sec) said in a debt market update on Tuesday.

"Over the past two to three weeks, rupee liquidity in the banking system has been augmented by Reserve Bank of India (RBI) spot dollar purchases in the forex market and this, to a certain extent, will dilute the impact of advance tax outflow," it said.
The improved liquidity conditions with banks have restricted the call rates "even in the month of March," a dealer with state-run bank said.
"Every year in the month of March it becomes difficult for the banking system to control the rising call rates," he said.

"There is plenty of liquidity in the system," Roopesh Pathania, a dealer at Barclays bank said. "The Reserve Bank's purchase of $700 million since the announcement of budget has eased the money condition to some extent," he said.
But if the call rates cross 7.0-8.0 percent, the repo auctions will attract less bidders, which again may boost liquidity by about 16.0 billion rupees, Pathania said.
The advance tax outflows may not impact the securities market much as banks are required to mark to market 50 percent of their trasury bills and government securities portfolio, dealers said.
"So it is unlikely banks will make fresh positions."
